main_body: A T-shaped timber post: a horizontal crossbeam (rows 9-17) on top of a thin vertical post (rows 18-47)
top_band: Crossbeam rows 10-12 (L=157 orange) then a cream highlight at row 13, then the darker face at rows 14-15. The orange rows could count as a top, but the band is a flat stripe, and the post below has no top or base surface.
evidence: The crossbeam shows a 3-row light band, a cream edge line at row 13 and a darker face, so it reads as a small 3/4 beam. The post is a 3px-wide vertical strip drawn flat from the front, with no top or base surface. The whole piece is a flat 2D T-shape, like a signpost or mallet seen face-on. The frame has no horizontal surfaces visible from above beyond the thin beam, and the base is missing. In doubt, fail.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and no full tile reaches the references' median of 17-20 colours per tile. The shading is shallow: the post is a flat mid-brown with one lighter stripe, and the beam has an orange band, a cream line and a brown band. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which is good. The piece is much simpler and thinner than the stall and the well, so it would look flatter next to them.
